claims.text: Integrating LLMs into information retrieval systems introduces emerging challenges regarding bias and unfairness.
Bias and unfairness issues in LLM-integrated information retrieval systems can be unified as distribution mismatch problems.
Mitigation strategies for bias and unfairness in LLM-integrated information retrieval systems can be categorized through distribution alignment.
Bias and unfairness issues arise across three distinct stages of LLM integration into information retrieval systems: data collection, model development, and result evaluation.

evidence.description: This evolution, while heralding new opportunities, introduces emerging challenges, particularly in terms of biases and unfairness, which may threaten the information ecosystem.
We first unify bias and unfairness issues as distribution mismatch problems...
...providing a groundwork for categorizing various mitigation strategies through distribution alignment.

Subsequently, we systematically delve into the specific bias and unfairness issues arising from three critical stages of LLMs integration into IR systems: data collection, model development, and result evaluation.

methodologies.name: Distribution Mismatch Survey and Taxonomy Framework
methodologies.description: A systematic literature review and taxonomy organizing bias, unfairness, and mitigation techniques in LLM-integrated IR systems through the lens of distribution mismatch and alignment across three system stages.

future_work.text: Address open problems and challenges to better understand and mitigate bias and unfairness issues in information retrieval systems in the LLM era.
